findings.evidence: PeterWeyl.lean:562 `∑' x, star (peterWeylCoeff models f x) * ...` vs PeterWeyl.lean:512 `∫ g : G, (starRingEnd 𝕜) (...)`; every scalar conjugation elsewhere in Compact/ uses `starRingEnd` (Convolution.lean:141, MatrixCoefficient.lean:115,171, Character/Basic.lean:125), `star (…)` only on `C(G,𝕜)`.
findings.fix: State it as `∑' x, (starRingEnd 𝕜) (peterWeylCoeff models f x) * peterWeylCoeff models g x = inner 𝕜 f g` (renaming to `tsum_conj_peterWeylCoeff_mul_peterWeylCoeff`); the proof already goes through `starRingEnd_apply`.
findings.issue: `tsum_star_peterWeylCoeff_mul_peterWeylCoeff` writes the scalar conjugate as `star (peterWeylCoeff models f x)`. `RCLike.star_def : (Star.star : K → K) = conj` is `@[simp]` (mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/RCLike/Basic.lean:381-383), so simp rewrites any goal into `starRingEnd 𝕜`, and this lemma's LHS never matches for `rw`/`simp`. The rest of the file — including `peterWeylCoeff` itself at line 512 — uses `(starRingEnd 𝕜)`.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/l2Space.lean:462 `HilbertBasis.hasSum_inner_mul_inner` and :468 `summable_inner_mul_inner` exist; the PR uses only :472 `tsum_inner_mul_inner` (PeterWeyl.lean:570).
findings.fix: Add `hasSum_star_peterWeylCoeff_mul_peterWeylCoeff` from `HilbertBasis.hasSum_inner_mul_inner` (same `simpa only [hfirst, ← repr_apply_apply, peterWeylBasis_repr_apply]` proof), derive the `tsum` form via `.tsum_eq`, and add the `Summable` corollary.
findings.issue: The polarized Parseval identity is given only in `tsum` form, so consumers get no summability of `x ↦ conj (c_f x) * c_g x` and cannot manipulate the series. The norm-square side ships all three forms (`hasSum_norm_sq_peterWeylCoeff` 574, `tsum_norm_sq_peterWeylCoeff` 582, `summable_norm_sq_peterWeylCoeff` 589), so the file already develops both sides of this trio.

summary: Prior findings are resolved: `peterWeylCoeff_def` and the unconditional `peterWeylCoeff_eq_inner` are present and the non-normal-form std expansion is gone; `peterWeylCoeff_def` should stay, since the body is unexposed. Remaining: the polarized Parseval statement conjugates with `star` on an `RCLike` scalar (not simp-normal) and ships without the `HasSum`/`Summable` forms that the norm-square side has.
